page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a large woodcut initial at the start of Thesis I; no marginal notes; page number at the head; catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.l: Disputatio Theologica,
De Perfectione SS. Scriptura.
Thesis I.
PErfectio Sacrae Scripturae est,
ejus omnimoda sufficientia in
tradenda tota voluntate divi-
na, qua spectat ad bene bea-
téque vivendum.
II. Quia autem haec perfectio vel
sufficientia prout absolutè sonat, tam qualitati-
vum, quàm quantitatum est, sive tam
extensivam, quàm extensivam plenitudinem
sufficientiae notat; nos imprasentiarum de
extensiva aut quantitativa perfectione sus acturi.
III. Possumus autem hanc perfection-
em Sacrae Scripturae concipere, tum qua
in se perfecta, tum qua talis est respectu
directionis atque institutionis nostrae. Est ea
perfecta in se, 1. quia nihil addi vel potest
debet, ac proinde est undequaque perfecta,
Psal. 19. vers. 8. Doctrina Jehovae integra
est restituens animam, Deut. 9. v. 2, nec
dite ad verbum illud quod ego praecipio vobis,

page.notes: Woodcut initial "P" at the start of Thesis I. Page numbering "1" printed at the head. Text is partly damaged at the left edge and some words are doubtful: "qualitativum"/"quantitatum", "extensivam", "sus acturi" and "dite" are uncertain readings; "nec dite" is probably a broken "nec addite". Final line ends with "vobis," and a signature "A 2" at the foot.
